title: Custom WordPress Build for Magazine
description:
The project

I'm building a German-language magazine on longevity, fitness, nutrition and sleep — evidence-based, editorial in tone, aimed at an educated and sceptical audience.

The defining feature is a transparent evidence rating: every article, glossary term and recommendation carries a visible rating of how solid the underlying science actually is. It is what separates the site from the usual supplement marketing, and building that component well is the heart of this job.

This is a private long-term project, not agency work. It's already carefully thought through — I've written the brief, the content model and the mockups myself, and I have roughly 360 finished glossary entries waiting to be imported.

The interesting part

The evidence rating is not a badge you drop in a template. It is:

Five states — three of them points on an evidence scale (solid / promising / hype), two of them orthogonal categories that deliberately render differently.
Three rendering variants from a single source value: a compact inline chip (automatic, appears wherever an item is listed), a header badge (automatic, one per article), and a detailed in-body callout (placed manually by me, mid-article).
Taxonomy-driven, not post meta — so listings and category hubs can filter by it cheaply.
A Gutenberg block with server-side render, plus an equivalent shortcode fallback. Both are needed: I draft articles as Markdown outside WordPress and paste them in, and blocks don't survive a paste.
Built for volume. A supplement round-up routinely contains 15–20 callouts in one article, all referencing a single shared source-numbering namespace, with the anchor IDs owned by the sources block rather than the callouts. That constraint is where most implementations would break, and §4.2.2 of the brief spells it out.

If that reads as a fun problem rather than a headache, we'll probably get along.

Scope

I'd like to commission this in two phases, and I'd like the quote split accordingly.

Phase 1 — the magazine. Remove the existing demo content, build a custom editorial layout, article and category templates, seven categories with hub pages, menus, core pages, the complete evidence rating component, the German legal layer (cookie consent, Consent Mode v2 via GTM, self-hosted fonts, template-enforced disclaimers), and the performance baseline. Success criterion: I can publish articles properly.

Phase 2 — the two content systems.

Glossary: custom post type for 500+ terms, one indexable page per term, DefinedTerm / DefinedTermSet schema, thematic cluster hubs, A–Z index, lightweight instant filtering, and a re-runnable, idempotent CSV importer (I supply the content; matching on slug so corrections don't create duplicates).
Recommendations: custom post type for a curated affiliate section, with a per-entry toggle that drives rel="sponsored nofollow" and the advertising label automatically — because the site launches with plain links and I swap them for affiliate URLs later, once the networks approve me.

Plus handover documentation.

Explicit non-goals
No page builder. No Elementor, Divi, WPBakery. The article body is Gutenberg; a builder would mean maintaining the evidence component twice for no benefit.
No demo or starter-site import. The current GeneratePress "Journal" demo is being discarded, and I don't want a different one in its place.
No WooCommerce. The recommendations section links out to third parties — it is an editorial link collection, not a shop. No cart, no checkout, no payment.
No content writing. I write everything: articles, glossary, page copy.
No logo design. Already finalised.
Environment

Shared Apache hosting (ALL-INKL Premium), PHP 8.5, Zend OPcache only — no Redis, no server-side page cache, no CDN. Core Web Vitals still matter to me, so caching strategy and image delivery need actual thought rather than a default plugin install. The tariff includes real cron jobs, SSH and full .htaccess access, all currently unused. §11 of the brief covers this in detail.

All custom functionality must live in a site-specific plugin, not the theme, so it survives a theme change.

One requirement I care about more than usual

After handover I must be able to maintain the site myself. Adding glossary terms, correcting entries, swapping affiliate URLs — all of it without hiring a developer each time.

Concretely: labelled German fields with helper text, list views with sortable columns and filters, bulk edit, and a short written guide. A system only its author can operate is not a finished system, and §8.5 and §9.2 of the brief make this an acceptance criterion rather than a preference.

What you get
A brief that has already answered the awkward questions — data model, naming, edge cases, failure modes, accessibility, schema, legal. You should have to guess very little.
HTML mockups as visual reference. They're direction, not a pixel contract; sensible UX improvements are welcome.
No deadline. Genuinely none. This is a personal project — you can fit it around urgent paid work, and I'd rather have it done well over several weeks than rushed.
Follow-up work if the collaboration goes well. I have further projects planned, including a searchable studio map and a premium listing service.
What I'm looking for in you
Comfortable writing custom WordPress code — custom post types, taxonomies, a Gutenberg block with block.json and server-side render, template hierarchy, a CSV importer.
Understands structured data and why DefinedTerm and additionalProperty are the right choices here.
Takes accessibility seriously — WCAG AA is a requirement in this brief, not a wish.
Willing to push back where you disagree with the spec. The brief marks a dozen decisions as yours; I'd rather hear an argument than get silent compliance.
How to apply

Two things, and please skip the generic pitch:

One specific question about the brief. Anything — a decision you'd make differently, an edge case you think I've missed, a constraint you'd challenge. It tells me far more than a portfolio does.
A quote split by phase (Phase 1 / Phase 2), plus a rough timeline for Phase 1.

If you'd also answer the questions in §16, that's ideal — but the one question above matters most.

title: Custom WordPress Build for Magazine
description:
The project

I'm building a German-language magazine on longevity, fitness, nutrition and sleep — evidence-based, editorial in tone, aimed at an educated and sceptical audience.

Taxonomy-driven, not post meta — so listings and category hubs can filter by it cheaply.
A Gutenberg block with server-side render, plus an equivalent shortcode fallback. Both are needed: I draft articles as Markdown outside WordPress and paste them in, and blocks don't survive a paste.
Built for volume. A supplement round-up routinely contains 15–20 callouts in one article, all referencing a single shared source-numbering namespace, with the anchor IDs owned by the sources block rather than the callouts. That constraint is where most implementations would break, and §4.2.2 of the brief spells it out.

Success criterion: I can publish articles properly.

Phase 2 — the two content systems.

Glossary: custom post type for 500+ terms, one indexable page per term, DefinedTerm / DefinedTermSet schema, thematic cluster hubs, A–Z index, lightweight instant filtering, and a re-runnable, idempotent CSV importer (I supply the content; matching on slug so corrections don't create duplicates).

No content writing. I write everything: articles, glossary, page copy.
No logo design. Already finalised.
Environment

Core Web Vitals still matter to me, so caching strategy and image delivery need actual thought rather than a default plugin install. The tariff includes real cron jobs, SSH and full .htaccess access, all currently unused. §11 of the brief covers this in detail.

All custom functionality must live in a site-specific plugin, not the theme, so it survives a theme change.

What you get
A brief that has already answered the awkward questions — data model, naming, edge cases, failure modes, accessibility, schema, legal. You should have to guess very little.
HTML mockups as visual reference. They're direction, not a pixel contract; sensible UX improvements are welcome.
No deadline. Genuinely none. This is a personal project — you can fit it around urgent paid work, and I'd rather have it done well over several weeks than rushed.
Follow-up work if the collaboration goes well. I have further projects planned, including a searchable studio map and a premium listing service.
What I'm looking for in you
Comfortable writing custom WordPress code — custom post types, taxonomies, a Gutenberg block with block.json and server-side render, template hierarchy, a CSV importer.
Understands structured data and why DefinedTerm and additionalProperty are the right choices here.
Takes accessibility seriously — WCAG AA is a requirement in this brief, not a wish.
Willing to push back where you disagree with the spec. The brief marks a dozen decisions as yours; I'd rather hear an argument than get silent compliance.
How to apply

One specific question about the brief. Anything — a decision you'd make differently, an edge case you think I've missed, a constraint you'd challenge. It tells me far more than a portfolio does.
A quote split by phase (Phase 1 / Phase 2), plus a rough timeline for Phase 1.

If you'd also answer the questions in §16, that's ideal — but the one question above matters most.

One specific question about the brief. Anything — a decision you'd make differently, an edge case you think I've missed, a constraint you'd challenge. It tells me far more than a portfolio does.

If you'd also answer the questions in §16, that's ideal — but the one question above matters most.

title: WordPress Rebuild for Medical Practice — 14 Pages, Wireframes and Copy Provided
description:
We are rebuilding the website for an established ENT and audiology practice in Raleigh, NC (in operation since 1993). The current site is on a hosted builder platform and needs to be rebuilt on WordPress.

This is a BUILD engagement, not a design engagement. We are supplying finished wireframes, a locked sitemap, all written copy, and all photography. We are not looking for creative direction, discovery workshops, or a proposed redesign. We know what we want built. We need someone to build it accurately, cleanly, and on schedule.

If you would rather propose your own design approach, this is not the right fit and I would rather save us both the time.

WHAT WE NEED BUILT

14 core pages (full list attached), plus one reusable condition page template — custom post type or equivalent — with 3 populated example entries. We will populate the remaining 9 entries ourselves after handoff, which is also how we will verify the site is genuinely editable by a non-technical staff member.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

These are not optional and should be reflected in your bid.

• JSON-LD schema markup: MedicalClinic, Physician, and FAQPage types.

• A mapped 301 redirect file from every existing URL to its new destination. Not a catch-all redirect to the homepage. This site has 30+ years of domain history and we are not losing it on launch day.

• A third-party HIPAA-compliant form embedded on the appointment request page. No patient-submitted data may pass through WordPress native forms, plugin form handlers, or plaintext notification emails. We provide and pay for the form vendor; you implement the embed and confirm the data path.

• WCAG 2.1 AA conformance. Our patient population skews 65+ with hearing and balance impairment. Verify contrast ratios, test at 200% browser zoom, no hover-dependent navigation, touch targets at 44px minimum, text alternatives on all images.

• Mobile-first responsive across current browsers, Core Web Vitals passing on mobile at launch.

• Google Analytics 4 and Search Console configured, with no advertising or social pixels on the appointment request page.

• SSL, XML sitemap, and robots.txt configured correctly. Note: the current site carries noindex tags that must not carry over.

NOT IN SCOPE

• Copywriting (we provide).
• Photography, logo, or brand design (we provide).
• E-commerce, cart, or payment processing.
• Ongoing SEO, content marketing, or maintenance retainer — may be discussed separately after launch.

DELIVERABLES AT HANDOFF

• Site live on hosting we own, under an admin account we own.

• Admin credentials transferred; no builder-retained access required for us to edit.

• A short written or recorded walkthrough (10–15 minutes) showing our office manager how to edit page
content, hours, and provider bios.

• The redirect map as a file.

• Documented list of plugins used and why.

TIMELINE AND BUDGET

4 to 6 weeks from kickoff. All copy and images will be ready before we start.
$2,800 to $4,000 fixed price, structured across 3 milestones. Please quote the full scope above. If something would push you past that range, tell me which item and what it would cost — I would rather hear that up front than discover it at milestone two.

TO APPLY

Please answer the screening questions. Applications that lead with a generic agency pitch and do not reference the specifics above will not be reviewed.

SCREENING QUESTIONS

1. Which theme or page builder would you use, and can a non-technical office manager edit page content, hours, and staff bios without touching the builder interface?

2. Walk me through how you handle 301 redirect mapping when rebuilding a site with existing URL structure and search history.

3. Have you embedded a third-party HIPAA-compliant form (Jotform HIPAA, Formstack Health, IntakeQ, or similar) into a client site? Which vendor, and how did you verify no submission data touched the CMS?

4. Please link me to a site you have built where the primary audience was over 65 or had accessibility requirements. If you have not built one, say so directly and tell me how you would approach it.

5. This is a fixed-price bid on the scope above. What specifically would trigger additional cost?

title: Senior WordPress & Elementor Designer Needed for Personal Brand Website
description:
# Senior WordPress & Elementor Designer Needed for Personal Brand Website

## Summary

I'm looking for an experienced **WordPress & Elementor designer/developer** to design and build a premium personal brand website.

This isn't a corporate website or a simple portfolio. The website should establish authority, communicate expertise, and convert visitors into booked calls and qualified leads.

The visual style should feel modern, clean, and editorial. I'm looking for someone with a strong eye for typography, spacing, composition, and user experience—not someone who relies on pre-made Elementor templates.

I value thoughtful design decisions and attention to detail.

---

## About the Brand

The website belongs to a business owner and consultant who works with established companies to help them grow and solve operational challenges.

The brand should communicate:

* Credibility
* Experience
* Professionalism
* Trust
* Clarity

The design should feel premium without becoming flashy or overdesigned.

---

## Pages

The website will consist of approximately **7–9 pages**, including:

* Home
* About
* Services
* Case Studies
* Blog
* Testimonials
* Contact
* Privacy Policy
* Terms & Conditions

---

## Scope of Work

You'll be responsible for both the design and development.

Responsibilities include:

* Designing a completely custom website in Elementor Pro
* Developing the approved design in WordPress
* Building reusable templates and global styles
* Creating a responsive experience across desktop, tablet, and mobile
* Implementing subtle animations where appropriate
* Designing layouts that keep visitors engaged without feeling cluttered
* Setting up forms and call-to-action sections
* Optimizing loading speed and Core Web Vitals
* Following SEO best practices
* Testing across major browsers before launch

The finished website should be easy for me to edit without needing a developer for routine updates.

---

## Design Direction

I'm looking for a designer who understands modern personal brand websites.

Some characteristics I'm looking for:

* Strong visual hierarchy
* Excellent typography
* Plenty of whitespace
* Premium imagery
* Editorial-style layouts
* Clear calls to action
* Smooth but subtle animations
* Clean navigation
* Consistent spacing throughout

Please do **not** submit websites that look like generic Elementor templates.

---

## Technical Requirements

* WordPress
* Elementor Pro
* Responsive development
* HTML/CSS knowledge
* Basic JavaScript (where needed)
* Fast loading times
* SEO-friendly structure
* Reusable templates
* Global colors & typography
* Easy-to-maintain backend

---

## Ideal Candidate

I'm looking for someone who:

* Has extensive Elementor experience
* Has a strong design portfolio
* Understands conversion-focused websites
* Pays attention to small design details
* Communicates clearly
* Delivers work on time
* Can recommend improvements where appropriate

This project may lead to ongoing work as I regularly build websites for businesses.

---

## When Applying

Please include:

1. A short introduction.
2. Links to **3 personal brand or service-based websites** you've personally designed and built.
3. Tell me exactly what your role was on each project (design, development, or both).
4. Your estimated timeline for completing this project.
5. What you believe separates a premium Elementor website from an average one.

**Applications without a portfolio will not be considered.**

description:
We are rebuilding the website for an established ENT and audiology practice in Raleigh, NC (in operation since 1993). The current site is on a hosted builder platform and needs to be rebuilt on WordPress.

This is a BUILD engagement, not a design engagement. We are supplying finished wireframes, a locked sitemap, all written copy, and all photography. We are not looking for creative direction, discovery workshops, or a proposed redesign. We know what we want built. We need someone to build it accurately, cleanly, and on schedule.

If you would rather propose your own design approach, this is not the right fit and I would rather save us both the time.

WHAT WE NEED BUILT

14 core pages (full list attached), plus one reusable condition page template — custom post type or equivalent — with 3 populated example entries. We will populate the remaining 9 entries ourselves after handoff, which is also how we will verify the site is genuinely editable by a non-technical staff member.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

These are not optional and should be reflected in your bid.

• JSON-LD schema markup: MedicalClinic, Physician, and FAQPage types.

• A mapped 301 redirect file from every existing URL to its new destination. Not a catch-all redirect to the homepage. This site has 30+ years of domain history and we are not losing it on launch day.

• A third-party HIPAA-compliant form embedded on the appointment request page. No patient-submitted data may pass through WordPress native forms, plugin form handlers, or plaintext notification emails. We provide and pay for the form vendor; you implement the embed and confirm the data path.

• WCAG 2.1 AA conformance. Our patient population skews 65+ with hearing and balance impairment. Verify contrast ratios, test at 200% browser zoom, no hover-dependent navigation, touch targets at 44px minimum, text alternatives on all images.

• Mobile-first responsive across current browsers, Core Web Vitals passing on mobile at launch.

• Google Analytics 4 and Search Console configured, with no advertising or social pixels on the appointment request page.

• SSL, XML sitemap, and robots.txt configured correctly. Note: the current site carries noindex tags that must not carry over.

NOT IN SCOPE

• Copywriting (we provide).
• Photography, logo, or brand design (we provide).
• E-commerce, cart, or payment processing.
• Ongoing SEO, content marketing, or maintenance retainer — may be discussed separately after launch.

DELIVERABLES AT HANDOFF

• Site live on hosting we own, under an admin account we own.

• Admin credentials transferred; no builder-retained access required for us to edit.

• A short written or recorded walkthrough (10–15 minutes) showing our office manager how to edit page
content, hours, and provider bios.

• The redirect map as a file.

• Documented list of plugins used and why.

TIMELINE AND BUDGET

4 to 6 weeks from kickoff. All copy and images will be ready before we start.
$2,800 to $4,000 fixed price, structured across 3 milestones. Please quote the full scope above. If something would push you past that range, tell me which item and what it would cost — I would rather hear that up front than discover it at milestone two.

3. Have you embedded a third-party HIPAA-compliant form (Jotform HIPAA, Formstack Health, IntakeQ, or similar) into a client site? Which vendor, and how did you verify no submission data touched the CMS?

4. Please link me to a site you have built where the primary audience was over 65 or had accessibility requirements. If you have not built one, say so directly and tell me how you would approach it.

# Senior Full-Stack E-Commerce Architect / Lead Developer Needed

## Existing React Frontend + Backend Development

### PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING

This is **not** a simple WooCommerce, Shopify, or WordPress website project.

If your experience is primarily installing plugins, customizing themes, or building basic template-based websites, this project is not the right fit.

We are looking for a **senior-level full-stack e-commerce developer or architect** who can review an existing React application, recommend the correct backend architecture, and complete the remaining development and integrations.

We need someone who can make strong technical decisions and build custom functionality—not someone who will need to learn on the job.

## Project Overview

The customer-facing frontend has already been built in **React**.

We now need an experienced developer to review the existing application and determine the best backend architecture before completing development.

Possible solutions may include:

* Headless WooCommerce
* Supabase
* A custom Node.js or other backend
* A hybrid architecture
* Another solution you recommend

We are not committed to one specific platform. We want the developer to recommend the best long-term solution based on:

* Scalability
* Performance
* Security
* Maintainability
* Payment integrations
* Shipping and fulfillment integrations
* Inventory management
* Ease of administration

A detailed developer specification packet outlining the required features will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

## Timeline and Budget

This is a **fixed-price project**, not an hourly position.

Several senior U.S.-based developers have reviewed our scope of work and developer specification packet and estimated the project at approximately **20 hours of development work for a skilled senior developer**.

We are therefore looking for someone with comparable experience and efficiency who can complete the project in approximately **20 hours or less**.

Our target is to have the project completed within approximately **one week of the start date**.

We are not looking for a developer who plans to stretch this project over one to three months. Please apply only if you have the senior-level experience, availability, and technical ability to complete the project within the requested timeline.

**Fixed project budget: Up to $2,000.**

Please do not submit an hourly proposal. Your proposal should include your complete fixed-price quote for the project.

The timeline and estimate assume that no major undisclosed problems are discovered in the existing React codebase during the initial review.

## Initial Technical Review

The selected developer will first review the existing React application and developer packet.

The initial review should include:

* Reviewing the existing codebase and architecture
* Identifying what has already been completed
* Identifying what still needs to be built
* Evaluating the quality and usability of the existing code
* Recommending the best backend architecture
* Explaining how the frontend and backend should communicate
* Recommending the database structure
* Recommending the payment gateway architecture
* Recommending the shipping and fulfillment architecture
* Identifying any security or scalability concerns
* Providing a clear implementation plan

The technical review is intended to confirm the architecture and identify any major issues—not to delay the project for weeks.

## Required Platform Functionality

The completed platform will require functionality including:

* Product management
* Product pricing and promotional pricing
* Product bundles
* Inventory tracking
* Low-stock notifications
* Lot and batch tracking
* Manufacturing-date tracking
* Expiration-date tracking
* Certificate of Analysis management
* COA assignment by product or lot
* Customer accounts
* Secure checkout
* Custom payment gateway integration
* Order management
* Order-status updates
* Automated customer emails
* Shipping-label integration
* Shipment tracking
* Shipping notifications
* 3PL or fulfillment integration
* Administrative dashboard
* Sales and inventory reporting
* Refund and cancellation management
* User permissions
* Security and fraud-prevention measures
* Mobile-responsive functionality
* Additional custom backend features outlined in our developer packet

## Required Experience

Applicants should have strong experience with:

* React
* JavaScript
* TypeScript
* Node.js
* REST APIs
* Webhooks
* E-commerce architecture
* Custom backend development
* WooCommerce
* Headless WooCommerce
* WordPress backend development
* Supabase
* PostgreSQL
* PHP
* Payment gateway integrations
* Shipping APIs
* Inventory-management systems
* Custom administrative dashboards
* Authentication and user-account systems
* Secure database architecture

Experience with all possible backend platforms is not required, but you must have enough architecture experience to evaluate the options objectively and recommend the best solution.

## Preferred Experience

Additional preferred experience includes:

* Headless e-commerce platforms
* High-risk merchant-processing integrations
* Custom payment processors
* Warehouse or 3PL integrations
* UPS, FedEx, USPS, or other shipping APIs
* Cloud deployment
* Database security
* Performance optimization
* E-commerce reporting systems
* Production application deployment

## Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for someone who:

* Has senior-level full-stack development experience
* Can understand an existing codebase quickly
* Can make independent architectural decisions
* Can clearly explain technical recommendations
* Writes clean, secure, maintainable code
* Communicates consistently
* Can begin promptly
* Can dedicate enough time to complete the project within approximately one week
* Is comfortable working under a fixed-price agreement
* Is interested in ongoing development work after the initial launch

This may become a long-term relationship for future features, maintenance, improvements, and additional projects.

## Application Instructions

Please answer all of the following questions in your proposal:

1. How many years have you worked with React?
2. Have you built a headless e-commerce platform?
3. Have you connected a React frontend to WooCommerce, Supabase, or a custom backend?
4. Have you integrated a custom payment gateway?
5. Have you integrated shipping or fulfillment APIs?
6. Have you built an inventory-management system?
7. Have you worked with lot, batch, expiration-date, or document-tracking functionality?
8. What backend architecture would you initially consider for this project, and why?
9. How would you approach reviewing the existing React application?
10. Please provide links or examples of similar projects.
11. What is your complete fixed-price quote?
12. How many development hours do you estimate?
13. What is your earliest available start date?
14. Can you complete the project within approximately one week?
15. Can you dedicate the necessary time to complete the work without stretching it over several weeks?

To confirm that you read the complete job posting, begin your proposal with:

**REACT COMMERCE ARCHITECT**

Applications that do not begin with this phrase may not be reviewed.
